# EDA — PSTU Data Thon 2026 Vol-1 (Stage 1, complete)

Single-file export of `dataset_exploration/` — every finding, every report, every generated
data table, consolidated so this can be read and shared standalone without the separate
script/report pairs. Nothing below is trimmed or summarized away from the source reports;
where a script produced a full CSV table (numeric describe, zero-inflation ratios, duplicate
groups, threshold sweeps), the complete table is embedded, not a sample of it.

**Source of truth:** `dataset_exploration/01_schema_dtypes.py` through `08_leak_diagnostics.py`
(numbered, idempotent scripts, each writing its own `*_report.txt` and, where relevant, a
`*.csv`), plus `dataset_exploration/README.md`. All numbers here are **measured** on the real
competition data on 2026-08-09 — none are carried over from `works.old/` or from `CLAUDE.md`'s
original first-pass profile. Local environment had pandas/numpy/scikit-learn only — script 07
uses `RandomForestClassifier` as a stand-in for the real LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost used later on Kaggle, per this project's convention.

Competition: predict `TARGET` (financial account flagged at-risk), binary classification, 350
anonymized features, evaluated with the F1 score (later independently confirmed to be **binary**
F1 via a live leaderboard probe — see Section 7 and `CLAUDE.md`).

## Executive summary (headline findings)

**Shape / schema** — confirmed exactly as CLAUDE.md's first pass stated: train 76,020×351
(350 `feat_*` + `TARGET`), test 60,654×351 (350 `feat_*` + `id` last), zero missing values,
212 int64 / 132 float64 / 6 object columns, positive rate 3.9569% (3,008/76,020).

**Categorical columns** — the 6 string columns' cardinality and train/test overlap match
CLAUDE.md's first pass exactly (feat_142: 2,333 train levels / 55 test-only; feat_325: 1,710 /
27; feat_157: 627 / 8; feat_320/337/318: 0 test-only). Every column's values match its expected
prefix 100%. All 6 have some test rows with unseen levels — any encoding needs an explicit
unseen-level fallback (see Section 2 for a per-scheme recipe).

**Sentinels — one new finding CLAUDE.md missed.** `feat_109 == -999999` confirmed as the sole
carrier of that fingerprint (116 train rows / 89 test rows, ~0.15%). `feat_169`'s extreme min
(~-1.11e8) is **not** a sentinel — it's a continuum of large-magnitude values with no repeated
constant, just genuine heavy-tailed data.
**New:** a second sentinel, exactly **`9999999999`** (1e10−1), appears across **23 columns**
(`feat_11, feat_21, feat_26, feat_30, feat_31, feat_36, feat_74, feat_77, feat_96, feat_124,
feat_135, feat_144, feat_149, feat_158, feat_171, feat_196, feat_204, feat_226, feat_301,
feat_315, feat_330, feat_336, feat_340`) — the classic Santander `delta_imp_*` fingerprint.
Same treat-as-missing logic should apply. **This was not in CLAUDE.md's first pass and was
added afterward.**

**Zero-inflation** — 252 of the **344 numeric** columns (not 350 — 6 of the 350 total feature
columns are the categorical strings) are ≥90% zero. CLAUDE.md's original phrasing ("252 of 350
numeric columns") was imprecise; the denominator should read 344.

**Constant + duplicate columns — CLAUDE.md's original headline number did not reproduce.**
- Constant-in-both train+test: **28** — matches CLAUDE.md's first pass exactly, same column list.
- Constant-in-test-only (kept, varies in train): **14** — matches CLAUDE.md's first pass exactly.
- **Exact-duplicate columns** (row-for-row identical values, excluding the constant columns
  above): **16 groups, all size 2, 16 redundant columns.** Combined droppable = 28 + 16 = **44**,
  not CLAUDE.md's original claimed 83 (28 + 55 across 20 groups).
- A looser **near-duplicate check** (`|corr| > 0.999`, columns that are scaled/linear copies of
  each other rather than byte-identical) finds 36 groups / 49 redundant columns → 77 combined,
  closer to but still short of 83. CLAUDE.md's 55/20 figure was likely produced by a
  correlation-based method at a different threshold and is not exactly reproducible.
- **Recommendation:** drop the 44 exact-duplicate/constant columns safely. Treat the
  corr>0.999 near-duplicate groups (Section 4) as dimensionality-reduction candidates only, not
  automatic drops — a scaled copy can still carry distinct information a tree model exploits.

**Adversarial validation** — 5-fold CV AUC discriminating train vs test = **0.5742 ± 0.0027**.
This is a **real, moderate covariate shift**, not the ~0.50 "safe iid split" CLAUDE.md's category
didn't originally measure. `feat_182` alone carries by far the most train/test separability
(importance 0.17, ~2.4x the next feature). 93/344 numeric columns have test values outside
their train range (`feat_116`, `feat_44`, `feat_334` worst offenders — all also top adversarial
features). **Recommendation:** watch CV-vs-LB gap; consider adversarial-validation sample
weighting or capping/clipping the worst out-of-range features before modeling.

**Duplicate rows / label conflicts** — confirmed **zero** duplicate feature-rows in train,
**zero** in test, **zero** rows shared between train and test on features alone. Matches
CLAUDE.md's first pass exactly. No label-conflict diagnostic needed (nothing to conflict).

**Metric behaviour** — degenerate floors:

| Submission | Binary F1 | Macro F1 |
|---|---|---|
| all zeros | 0.0000 | 0.4899 |
| all ones | 0.0761 | 0.0381 |

The all-zeros LB probe (≈0.49 → macro F1, ≈0.00 → binary F1) was the right first move — and,
per `CLAUDE.md`, an actual live-leaderboard submission of all zeros later scored **0.0000000**,
confirming the grader uses **binary F1**. On a quick RF baseline (OOF AUC 0.8485) in this
script, the optimal threshold for both binary-F1 and macro-F1 landed at the same point (t=0.75
in that run) — the two objectives don't necessarily require different operating points, but
re-tune per model since this is not guaranteed to hold.

**Leak diagnostics — no leak found, real ceiling confirmed.**
- Row-index AUC: 0.5047 (no leak from row order; positive rate is flat ~3.4–4.5% across all
  10 index blocks).
- Best single-feature AUC: 0.6986 (`feat_175`) — no magic feature (would expect >0.85 if leaked).
- Capacity test (unregularized `DecisionTreeClassifier`): train AUC 1.0000 (expected — full
  memorization), held-out val AUC 0.5916, gap 0.41. Val AUC collapses relative to train →
  normal overfitting, **no deterministic rule exists** → the score has a genuine ceiling to
  push against, unlike the old withdrawn dataset.
- Duplicate-row label consistency: N/A (zero duplicate rows exist to conflict).

=== Recommended unseen-level handling ===
All 6 columns have test rows with levels not present in train (see pct_unseen above).
Any encoding scheme MUST map unseen-at-inference levels to a reserved bucket rather
than erroring or NaN-ing:
  - target/frequency encoding: map unseen level -> global train mean / 0 count, not NaN
  - one-hot / ordinal (sklearn): use handle_unknown='ignore' / an explicit UNK category
  - tree models fed raw codes: fit a LabelEncoder-like mapping on train, unseen -> -1
This must be validated by refitting only on train and transforming test with fitted
mapping (never fit on train+test concatenated, which leaks the level identity).

## 7. Metric behaviour

**Script:** `dataset_exploration/07_metric_behaviour.py` — binary-F1 vs macro-F1 degenerate
floors, threshold sweep.

```text
positive rate: 0.039569 (3008/76020)

=== Degenerate floors: binary F1 vs macro F1 ===
submission       binary_f1    macro_f1
all zeros           0.0000      0.4899
all ones            0.0761      0.0381

=== Diagnostic probe recommendation ===
Submit all-zeros as an early LB probe.
  LB ~= 0.4899 -> grader is using MACRO F1.
  LB ~= 0.0000 -> grader is using BINARY F1.
This single submission resolves the contradiction in the competition page and
determines the entire thresholding strategy downstream.

=== Quick OOF baseline (RandomForest, 5-fold, NOT the final model) ===
OOF ROC-AUC (threshold independent): 0.8485

=== Threshold sweep (0.02-0.98, step 0.01) -> 07_threshold_sweep.csv ===
Best threshold for BINARY F1: t=0.75  binary_f1=0.3104  macro_f1=0.6415
Best threshold for MACRO F1:  t=0.75  binary_f1=0.3104  macro_f1=0.6415
Naive t=0.5:                  binary_f1=0.2558  macro_f1=0.5868

Binary-F1 gain from tuning threshold vs naive 0.5: +0.0547
Macro-F1 gain from tuning threshold vs naive 0.5:  +0.0547

=== Recommendation ===
Run the diagnostic probe FIRST. Whichever metric it confirms, tune the decision
threshold on out-of-fold predictions to maximize that exact metric (binary_f1 or
macro_f1 from this sweep), not accuracy or AUC. Because the grader applies a fixed
0.5 cut to whatever is submitted, encode the chosen operating point as hard 0/1
labels (or rank-shift probabilities so the 0.5 cut lands at the tuned threshold).
Re-tune the threshold every time the model or feature set changes -- the optimum
is not stable across model versions.
```

**Later, real-world confirmation (recorded in `CLAUDE.md`, not part of this script's own
output):** an actual `all_zeros_submission.csv` was submitted to the live public leaderboard on
2026-08-09 and scored **0.0000000**, matching the binary-F1 floor above exactly. **The grader
uses binary F1**, settling the ambiguity this script flagged.
